clue.text: Female colour bar

parts.note: read not as racial segregation but as a bar, or stick, of colour that a woman applies to her mouth

explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic for the mouth comes as a small stick of colour, so it is literally a colour bar used by women.

clue.text: Keel over with thought-a non-practical one

parts.note: an idea is a thought
a ship that keels over leans, or lists

explanation.surface: A dreamer's theory topples someone over.
explanation.definitionFit: A visionary who pursues high principles rather than what is workable is unpractical.

clue.text: Bird dogs butterflies

parts.note: the swallow is a bird
to dog someone is to follow closely, to tail them

explanation.surface: A bird pursues butterflies through the air.
explanation.definitionFit: These large butterflies take their name from the long tail streamers on the hindwings.

clue.text: Intimation to end union amendment

indicators.note: an amendment alters a text, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A hint that a change will finish off the trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word; the letters of END UNION are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A veiled suggestion or insinuation is an indirect intimation.

clue.text: Inks out individual member of family tree'

indicators.note: out says the letters of inks are thrown out of order

parts.note: a man is an individual person

explanation.surface: Someone inks out one person's name from a genealogy chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges INKS into KINS, then MAN follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A blood relative belongs on the same genealogy.

clue.text: Foreign Office once turned to ward off affront

indicators.note: turned says the abbreviation is flipped round to read backwards

parts.note: FO was the abbreviation for the Foreign Office before it was renamed
to fend is to ward off

explanation.surface: A government department once moved to deflect an insult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks FO as the old abbreviation of Britain's Foreign Office; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To affront someone is to insult or upset them.

clue.text: Military order for home heat

explanation.surface: An army instruction about heating the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The command to shoot is a military order; a hearth blaze heats the home.

clue.text: Old campaigner could show a rude scar

indicators.note: could show says the letters can be rearranged to reveal something else

explanation.surface: A veteran fighter bears an ugly wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval knight on campaign to the Holy Land was an old campaigner; the word also means any zealous activist.

clue.text: Lower the status of Venus in world circles

definitions.text: the status of Venus in world circles

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to demote the goddess of love among high society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'world circles' sounds like social circles, but it means orbits: Venus circles the Sun inside the Earth's orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: Lower means lesser in rank; astronomers call Venus an inferior planet because its orbit lies inside the Earth's.

clue.text: Nominally she gets five years

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
an era is a long period of years

explanation.surface: A woman receives a five-year sentence, at least on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nominally she' asks for a woman's name rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's first name, so by name it stands for a particular she.

clue.text: Set pieces for sergeant-majors?

explanation.surface: Rehearsed football moves are being planned for drill instructors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set pieces' suggests football or theatre; here a set is a wireless receiver and its pieces are the parts that give out sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The parts of a radio or television set that produce sound; sergeant-majors bellow orders, so they are loud talkers.

clue.text: Makes a fuss spring cleaning?

explanation.surface: Someone complains loudly about the annual house clean.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for creating a commotion; literally, vigorous housework stirs up dirt.

clue.text: Deny this half being in the county

indicators.note: being in says the half-word sits inside the county's name

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland

indicators.note: half of the word this, its second half

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to accept that part of the county is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the back half of 'this', IS, which goes inside DOWN, a county of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclaim or refuse to acknowledge something as one's own is to deny it.

clue.text: Devoted dad cited in error

indicators.note: in error says the letters of these words have been set down wrongly and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A loyal father has been named by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone utterly given over to a habit or pursuit is hooked on it, devoted to it.

clue.text: Let be, boy! Should come to a head

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's instruction meaning let it stand
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A parent tells a child to leave things alone before a crisis erupts.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR read the exclamation mark as 'I'. 'come to a head' means reach a crisis, but here it is literal: a hat comes down onto the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy hat is made to sit on the head, so it should end up there.

clue.text: Non-nuclear chain reactor

parts.note: a chain reaction suggests atomic physics, but read it as a toothed wheel that reacts with a bicycle chain

explanation.definitionFit: A toothed wheel engaging the links of a chain drives or is driven by it.

clue.text: Old soldier in a Wonderland quadrille

explanation.surface: A veteran trooper joins a dance in a fairy-tale land.
explanation.walkthrough: In Alice's Adventures in Wonderland the Mock Turtle describes the Lobster Quadrille; British soldiers in red coats were called lobsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcoat soldiers were once nicknamed after the red shellfish, and Lewis Carroll's Alice hears of a dance named after the same creature.

clue.text: Recorder motored east as arranged

indicators.note: as arranged says the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A driver who motored east took a note of it as agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: The dashboard instrument records the distance a vehicle has travelled.

clue.text: Smooth waters late in the day

parts.note: even means smooth or level
the tide is the sea's waters rising and falling

explanation.surface: Calm seas at dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for evening, the close of the day.

clue.text: Benefits for going back in the mines

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: pits are coal mines

indicators.note: going back says the word for is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Miners return to the pits for the perks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns FOR into ROF, which goes 'in' PITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gains or returns from a venture are its benefits.

clue.text: Record a range of notes

explanation.surface: Someone documents a span of musical tones.
explanation.definitionFit: An official list or log is a record; in music the compass of a voice or instrument is its range.

clue.text: Saw the head — for examination purposes ?

definitions.text: Saw the head — for examination purposes ?

parts.words: Saw the head — for examination purposes ?
parts.note: Saw looks like the past of see, as if meeting the headmaster, but it means cutting into the skull, as a surgeon does

explanation.surface: A pupil visited the headteacher about exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' suggests a school head and 'examination' a test, but the surgery is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons bore or cut a hole in the skull with a crown saw to inspect or relieve the brain.

clue.text: Generous quarry for a bird

parts.note: OS is short for outsize, a generous size
quarry is the creature hunted, its prey

explanation.surface: A hunter generously offers its catch to a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is the clothing label for generous sizes; the fish hawk is itself a hunter, so the quarry fits the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish-eating hawk is one species of bird.

clue.text: Ideal place for a sit-down strike in the Midlands ?

definitions.text: Ideal place for a sit-down strike in the Midlands ?

parts.words: Ideal place for a sit-down strike in the Midlands ?
parts.note: a sit-down strike suggests a protest, but read it as a deep buttoned sofa to sit on, sharing its name with a Derbyshire mining town in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: Workers look for the best town in central England to stage a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Midlands is the central region of England; Derbyshire was coalfield country with a history of miners' strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep leather sofa named after a Derbyshire town is a comfortable seat, and the town lies in the Midlands mining country.

clue.text: Aquarius the wide-mouthed one as it were perhaps ?

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters of were may be shuffled into another word

explanation.surface: The water-carrier of the zodiac is described as having a wide mouth, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: Aquarius is the Water Carrier; 'as it' are link words and 'perhaps' rearranges WERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-mouthed jug carries water, like the zodiac's water-bearer.

clue.text: One the soldier returns to after leave

definitions.text: the soldier returns to after leave

explanation.surface: A soldier comes back to base once his time off ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' looks like a reversal signal but is plain English here.
explanation.definitionFit: A single thing counted as a whole is a one; a soldier on leave goes back to the regiment or company he serves in.

clue.text: Paper of reputable memory ?

explanation.surface: A newspaper with a fine reputation for remembering.
explanation.walkthrough: Paper sizes once had names such as foolscap and elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephant is an old size of drawing paper, and the large animal is proverbially said never to forget.

clue.text: Advanced vainly though well supported

explanation.surface: Someone moved forward with conceit despite plenty of backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To swagger forward is to walk proudly; a structure braced with props or struts is well supported.
